references.text: Jotham was the only one of Gideon's seventy sons who survived Abimelech's massacre by hiding
Jotham's speech from Mount Gerizim before he fled, where he told the parable of the trees and prophesied judgment against Abimelech and the men of Shechem
Jacob fled to Laban to escape his brother Esau's anger, a similar pattern of fleeing from a dangerous brother
Moses fled from Pharaoh and settled in Midian, a similar pattern of fleeing from a threat and settling elsewhere
David fled from Saul who sought his life, a similar pattern of fleeing from one who wanted to kill him
David fled and hid in the cave of Adullam to escape Saul, a parallel example of seeking refuge
